narrative_purpose: Shows why the same molecule is poison in one cell and fuel in another: identical machinery, different amount of it, and the electron chain either dark or running.
subject: Two elongated organelle studies side by side at high magnification, both the same shape and size, both showing a heavily folded inner membrane running lengthwise. On the left: the membrane is dark and inert, and a crowd of small pale sulfur particles is jammed against one large protein complex at the end of the membrane chain, that complex drained of light and dull. On the right: the same membrane glows bright teal along its whole length, and the same pale sulfur particles are being taken up by dense repeated arrays of a different, smaller protein form spaced along the membrane, from which bright motes stream onward into the glowing chain.
scene: A dark cytological specimen space, the two organelles floating as if pinned side by side for comparison, deep indigo beyond.
camera: Flat-on comparison view at matched scale, one organelle in each half of the frame, a clear dark gap between them.
light: Left organelle unlit except for a faint cold edge; right organelle lit from within by its own membrane glow; the surrounding space dark.
palette: Void-indigo ground, dead grey-teal and a touch of magenta on the left organelle, bright living-teal and cyan on the right, pale neutral for the sulfur particles in both halves.
style: Painterly naturalist cytological plate, oil texture, luminous biological key light, two studies in one consistent hand.
detail_level: Crisp on the membrane folds, on the jammed complex at left and on the repeated enzyme arrays at right; the outer membranes softer; frame edges dissolving into shadow.
composition: Symmetrical two-panel balance with a dark vertical gap down the centre, the blocked end-complex on the left half and the repeated enzyme arrays on the right half sitting at the same height for direct comparison.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette. Both organelles must be recognisably the same kind of structure - the difference is in illumination and in how many enzyme units line the membrane, never in anatomy. Keep the central gap and the space above both studies dark and plain for overlaid callouts.
negative_prompt: no text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no diagram lines, no panel borders, no flat vector art, no infographic styling, no UI, no watermarks, no 3D render
